title: Colour the open chords
summary: Small, unfamiliar shapes are the bottleneck, not knowledge. This level works the colours one finger away from the open chords you own — sus2, sus4, add9, maj7, 7, m7, 6 — and the few grips that will feel foreign at first: two thumb-over chords, Bm7(add11), Em7/G and the open sevenths. Fake Plastic Trees holds one grip while the bass moves under it, slowly; Here Comes the Sun (capo 7) adds sus hammer-ons and odd-meter bars. Session B starts numbers in C, G and D.
goals: Fake Plastic Trees with the record in the colour voicings (Dmaj9/F♯, Bm7(add11)).
Here Comes the Sun with the record (capo 7), sus hammer-ons on D and A, the 11/8 bridge counted.
Turn any open A, D, C or Am into its sus2, sus4, add9, maj7, 7, m7 or 6 relative by moving one finger, without looking.
Land the new grips — the two thumb chords, Bm7(add11), Em7/G, G7 and D7 — in one movement: 30+ clean changes a minute into each.
Play C, G and D major in open position, and name the six chords of each key (and the sevenths of C and G) by number.

song_plan: Core: **Fake Plastic Trees** (slow; one grip with the bass moving under it) and **Here Comes the Sun** (capo 7; faster, with odd-meter bars). A week's section already solid? Take the next week's. Swap a core song for an alternate only when you can already play it with the record, or when its hard change is still under 15 a minute after two weeks; keep that hard change in Session A either way. Alternates, easiest first: *Good Feeling* (sus decorations), *The Book of Love* (thumb D/F♯), *The First Cut Is the Deepest* (rock-G anchors).

exit_criteria: Benchmark pairs 1–4 at target (30 / 35 / 30 / 30 a minute) in two Session Ds in a row.
Fake Plastic Trees with the record, colour voicings, thumb chords clean, no stops.
Here Comes the Sun with the record, capo 7, bridge counted, no stops.
Colour lines 1–5 one bar per chord at 80 with eyes closed, every string clean.
G major open position up and down in eighths at 80, from memory; then the six chords of C, G and D saying the numbers, no hesitation.
stuck: Not every box ticked after 6 weeks? Move on anyway. Keep one song from this level (Fake Plastic Trees, or an easier alternate) as a 5-minute play-through in Level 2's Session D, and open every Level 2 Session A primer with your weakest pair until it reaches 30.
skip_ahead: Pass every benchmark cold (first attempt, no practice that day) in week 1's Session D? Go straight to Level 2 and keep both songs as Session D play-throughs.

drills.title: New-grip primer
drills.instructions: The level's genuinely new grips, each chosen because it breaks a habit your hand already has. **1 Thumb over:** Dmaj9/F♯ 2x0220 and D/F♯ 2x0232 — the thumb frets string 6 at fret 2 and its tip mutes string 5. **2 Spread grip:** Bm7(add11) x20230 — index on string 5, open strings between the fingers. **3 Back-to-front G:** Em7/G 322030 — ring on string 6, index on 5, little finger on 2. **4 Mirror sevenths:** G7 320001 and D7 xx0212 — the fingers sit in a different order from the G and D you know, so old habits pull them to the wrong strings. Each shape: air shape ×5, then place-and-lift ×10 at 60. About a minute per grip.

drills.title: One-minute changes
drills.instructions: Timer at 1:00. One down-strum per chord, change, strum the other, as fast as you can while staying clean. Count clean landings only: every string of the shape rings, no stray strings. Two rounds per pair; write the better count.

drills.title: Air shapes
drills.instructions: Hand off the neck. Form the whole shape an inch above the strings, land all fingers at once, strum once, check every string, lift. Ten per shape. On the thumb chords the thumb lands with the fingers, not after them.

drills.title: Place and lift
drills.instructions: Fret the shape, relax until the fingers just touch the strings, press again. Twenty presses, one per click at 60, no strumming. Use it on the new grips: the two thumb chords, Bm7(add11), Em7/G, G7 and D7.

drills.title: Anchor hunt
drills.instructions: Before a new pair, say aloud what stays (anchor), what slides along its string (guide) and what jumps. Then ten changes keeping anchors down and guides touching. This level: **A ↔ Dmaj9/F♯** = finger A index–middle–ring; middle and ring stay on strings 3–2, the index lifts, the thumb comes over. **A ↔ Bm7(add11)** = middle stays, index hops from string 4 to string 5, ring slides up to fret 3. **G7 ↔ Cmaj7** = ring and middle cross one string together, index lifts. **Em7/G → D/F♯** = string 2 fret 3 sounds in both: try keeping the little finger on it.

drills.title: Slow motion
drills.instructions: Make the change over a slow count of five, every finger moving at once on the shortest path. Watch the fingers. Five slow, then five at normal speed.

drills.title: Change loop
drills.instructions: Strum chord 1 once, change, strum chord 2 once, stop, reset. Ten clean in a row; a miss sets the count back to zero. For a line of three or four chords, loop the whole line.

drills.title: Tempo ladder
drills.instructions: One chord per bar, four down-strums. Start where the change is perfect (try 50). Three clean passes: +4 bpm. A miss: −8 bpm. Write the top clean tempo in today's blank.

drills.title: Bass first
drills.instructions: For the thumb chords (Dmaj9/F♯, D/F♯): on beat 1 play only the thumb's F♯ (string 6, fret 2), then strum the rest on beat 2. Ten times; then land the thumb first inside a single full strum.

drills.title: Eyes closed
drills.instructions: Make the change without looking. Open your eyes after landing to check. Ten times.

drills.title: Leave early
drills.instructions: Down-up eighths, four bars per chord. On the last “and” of each bar let go and strum the open strings while travelling. In Here Comes the Sun do it on every change; in Fake Plastic Trees, into the thumb chord.

drills.title: Song loop
drills.instructions: Loop the two bars around the hard change in the song's own rhythm, 10 bpm under this week's tempo. Then add a bar either side. Then the whole section.

drills.title: Random pairs
drills.instructions: Write the 16 chord names from the chord page on scraps of paper. Draw two, do one-minute changes, write the pair and the count on the back of the sheet. Draw again.

drills.title: Colour lines
drills.instructions: One bar per chord, four down-strums, metronome 70 → 90; only the named finger moves. **1 A:** x02220 → Asus4 x02230 (little finger on) → A → Asus2 x02200 (lift ring) → A. **2 D:** xx0232 → Dsus4 xx0233 (little finger on) → D → Dsus2 xx0230 (lift middle) → D. **3 D line:** D → Dmaj7 xx0222 → D7 xx0212 → D6 xx0202 — only the string-2 note moves (D C♯ C B), but the grip changes each time. **4 C:** x32010 → Cmaj7 x32000 (lift index) → C → C7 x32310 (little finger on) → C → Cadd9 x32030 (index off, little finger to string 2 fret 3) → C. **5 Minor:** Am x02210 → Am7 x02010 (lift ring) → Am; Em 022000 → Em7 022030 (little finger on) → Em.

drills.title: Scale in 3rds
drills.instructions: In this week's scale play pairs a 3rd apart: C–E, D–F, E–G, F–A, G–B, A–C, B–D, C–E … to the top, then back down (in G: G–B, A–C, B–D …). Quarters at 60 until clean, then eighths.

drills.title: Scale, then its chords
drills.instructions: Play the scale up and down once. Then strum the key's chords, one bar each, saying the numbers aloud. **C:** C Dm Em F G Am = I ii iii IV V vi. **Sevenths of C:** Cmaj7 x32000, Dm7 xx0211, Em7 022030, Fmaj7 xx3210, G7 320001, Am7 x02010 = Imaj7 iim7 iiim7 IVmaj7 V7 vim7. **G:** G Am Bm C D Em (Bm x24432). **Sevenths of G:** Gmaj7 320002, Am7 x02010, Bm7 x20202, Cmaj7 x32000, D7 xx0212, Em7 022030. **D:** D Em F♯m G A Bm (F♯m 244222). Then I–vi–IV–V in this week's key: C Am F G · G Em C D · D Bm G A.

drills.title: Sing and find the root
drills.instructions: Strum a chord. Hum its lowest note. Find that note on string 6 and on string 5 below fret 12, play it against the chord, say its name. Write the frets on the session page.

drills.title: Count 3+3+3+2
drills.instructions: Here Comes the Sun bridge. Metronome at 150 and call each click an eighth note. Say “1-2-3 1-2-3 1-2-3 1-2”, one strum on each “1”: F, C, G, D. Then one 4/4 bar of D and a 7/8 bar of A7 counted “1-2 1-2 1-2-3”. Five clean passes, then +10.

drills.title: Make something
drills.instructions: Pick a home chord (A or D). Choose three more shapes from the chord page. Loop them four beats each. Every pass change one thing: the order, one colour (sus2, sus4, maj7, 7 or 6), or the rhythm. Keep the version you'd want to play again; write it in the session's Notes line.

sessions.name: A
sessions.title: Chord day
sessions.focus: The new grips and this week's three pairs (week plan, column 1). Pair 1 is the hard one.

blocks.title: Primer: the new grips
blocks.instructions: Grips 1–4 from the drill page, thumb chords first: air shape ×5, then place-and-lift ×10 at 60, on each shape.

blocks.title: Pair 1: the full recipe
blocks.instructions: Anchor hunt (say what stays, slides, jumps) → slow motion ×5 → change loop to 10 clean → tempo ladder from 50, one chord per bar. Thumb chord in the pair? Bass first ×10 before the ladder. Stop at the clock even if it's going well.

blocks.title: Pairs 2 and 3
blocks.instructions: Change loop to 10 clean on each, then one-minute changes: two rounds each. Write the better count. A line of three or four chords? Loop the line and count clean passes.

blocks.title: Colour lines
blocks.instructions: Lines 1–5 from the drill page, one bar per chord. Last pass of lines 1, 2 and 4 with eyes closed.

blocks.title: Fretboard: this week's key
blocks.instructions: This week's scale once up and down in quarters at 60, then its chords one bar each, saying the numbers.

blocks.title: Song: put pair 1 back in
blocks.instructions: In the song pair 1 comes from (week 4: the song with more stops last Session D): song loop on the bars with the change, then this week's section ×3 at this week's tempo.

blocks.title: Log
blocks.instructions: Log page: tick A, write the minutes. In Notes: the change that felt worst today.

sessions.name: B
sessions.title: Fretboard day
sessions.focus: Scales and numbers in the open keys, then both songs by number (week plan, column 2).

blocks.title: Primer
blocks.instructions: Air shapes ×10 on the two chords of pair 1, then the same change with eyes closed ×10.

blocks.title: This week's scale
blocks.instructions: Say the root name every time you play a square. Quarters at 60 until clean, then eighths on the tempo ladder. Week 2: in 3rds as well.

blocks.title: Scale, then its chords
blocks.instructions: Scale once, then the key's chords one bar each, saying the numbers (weeks 2–3: the sevenths too). Then I–vi–IV–V in this week's key.

blocks.title: Find the bass line
instructions: Fake Plastic Trees' bass notes. Strum A, Dmaj9/F♯, E, Dsus2, Bm7(add11); hum each lowest note and find it on string 6 and string 5. Write the frets (string 6 / string 5):

blocks.title: Song by numbers: Fake Plastic Trees
blocks.instructions: Key of A: A = I, Dmaj9/F♯ = vi (it stands in for F♯m), E = V, Dsus2 = IV, Bm7(add11) = ii. Section A ×2 at this week's tempo, saying each number as you change. Then plain I–vi–V–IV in G (G Em D C) and C (C Am G F).

blocks.title: Song by numbers: Here Comes the Sun
blocks.instructions: Capo 7, D shapes = key of D. Verse D D G A7 = I I IV V7; the refrain's E7 = II7 (the V of V). Bridge F C G D = ♭III ♭VII IV I (three from outside the key). Verse ×2, refrain ×1 at this week's tempo, leaving early.

blocks.title: Log
blocks.instructions: Log page: tick B, write the minutes. Notes: anything in the scale you still have to look at.

sessions.name: C
sessions.title: Song day
sessions.focus: Longest song work: isolate this week's hard change (pair 1), then both songs in time at this week's tempos.

blocks.title: Primer
blocks.instructions: Place-and-lift ×20 and air shapes ×10 on the two chords of pair 1. Thumb chord in the pair? Bass first ×10 as well.

blocks.title: The hard change
blocks.instructions: Change loop to 10 clean, then tempo ladder one chord per bar from 50.

blocks.title: Fretboard: the bass under the songs
blocks.instructions: D major open position once, quarters at 60. Then only the bass notes of Fake Plastic Trees section A, one per bar, saying the numbers: A A A A · F♯ F♯ F♯ E · D A D D = 1 1 1 1 · 6 6 6 5 · 4 1 4 4.

blocks.title: Fake Plastic Trees
blocks.instructions: Song loop round the hard change if it is in this song (4 min). This week's section ×3 at this week's tempo. Then everything you have learned, without stopping — fumble through. Weeks 3–4: the last 4 minutes with the record.

blocks.title: Here Comes the Sun
blocks.instructions: Bridge: count 3+3+3+2 out loud, one strum per group — F C G D (3 min). Then this week's section ×2 with the sus hammer-ons on D and A, and the whole song without stopping, leaving early on every change. Weeks 3–4: with the record.

blocks.title: Log
blocks.instructions: Log page: tick C, write the minutes. Notes: the bar where you stopped, if any.

sessions.name: D
sessions.title: Mix and measure
sessions.focus: Short versions of everything, the benchmarks with numbers, and five minutes of your own music.

blocks.title: Primer
blocks.instructions: Air shapes ×5 on each chord in benchmarks 1–4 (log page). Nothing more — the tests are taken cold.

blocks.title: Benchmarks
blocks.instructions: One-minute changes, one round each, cold: **1** A ↔ Dmaj9/F♯ · **2** Bm7(add11) ↔ A · **3** Em7/G ↔ D/F♯ · **4** G7 ↔ Cmaj7. Then tempo ladders from 60: **5** colour line 3, one chord per beat; **6** G major open position in eighths. Write all six numbers in this week's column of the log.

blocks.title: Keys from memory
blocks.instructions: On the back of this sheet write the six chords of C, G and D with their numbers, and the sevenths of C. Check against the drill page. Then play G's six, eyes closed.

blocks.title: Songs, measured
blocks.instructions: Fake Plastic Trees, then Here Comes the Sun: with the record from week 3, at this week's tempo before that. Count the stops; write benchmarks 7 and 8 in the log.

blocks.title: Make something
blocks.instructions: Home chord A or D plus three shapes from the chord page, four beats each, looped. Each pass change one thing: order, one colour, or the rhythm. Write the keeper (chords and strum) in Notes.

blocks.title: Log and exit check
blocks.instructions: Tick D in the log. Tick any exit box you passed today. Week 6 or all boxes ticked? Fill in the check-in sheet.
